ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. I never came within these abbey walls, nor did you ever draw your sword on me. I never saw the chain, so help me heaven; and what you charge me with is false.

DUKE. Why, what an intricate charge this is! I think you've all drunk from Circe's cup. If you'd shut him in here, he'd have been here. If he were mad, he wouldn't plead so coolly. You say he dined at home — the goldsmith here denies that. Sirrah, what do you say?
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. Sir, he dined with her there, at the Porcupine.
COURTESAN. He did, and from my finger snatched that ring.
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. It's true, my liege — I had this ring from her.
DUKE. Did you see him enter the abbey here?
COURTESAN. As surely, my liege, as I see your Grace.
DUKE. Why, this is strange. Go, call the abbess here. I think you're all bewildered, or stark mad.
[Exit one to the Abbess.]
EGEON. Most mighty Duke, allow me to speak a word. I think I see a friend who will save my life and pay the sum that may free me.
DUKE. Speak freely, Syracusan, whatever you wish.
EGEON. Is not your name, sir, Antipholus? And isn't that your bondman Dromio?
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. Within this hour I was his bondman, sir, but he — thank him — gnawed in two my cords. Now I'm Dromio, and his man, unbound.
EGEON. I'm sure you both remember me.
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. We remember ourselves, sir, by looking at you — for lately we were bound the way you are now. You're not Pinch's patient, are you, sir?
EGEON. Why do you look at me as a stranger? You know me well.
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. I never saw you in my life until now.
EGEON. Oh, grief has changed me since you saw me last, and careful hours, with time's deformed hand, have written strange ravages on my face. But tell me yet — don't you recognize my voice?
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. Neither.
EGEON. Dromio, nor you?
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. No, trust me, sir, nor I.
EGEON. I'm sure you do.
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. Yes, sir, but I'm sure I don't — and whatever a man denies, you're now bound to believe him.

EGEON. Not know my voice! Oh, time's extremity, have you so cracked and split my poor tongue in seven short years that here my only son doesn't recognize my feeble key of untuned cares? Though now this furrowed face of mine is hidden by sap-consuming winter's drizzled snow, and all the channels of my blood frozen up, yet has my night of life some memory, my wasting lamps some fading glimmer left, my dull, deaf ears a little use for hearing. All these old witnesses — I cannot be wrong — tell me you are my son Antipholus.
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. I never saw my father in my life.
EGEON. But only seven years ago, in Syracuse, boy, you know we parted. But perhaps, my son, you're ashamed to acknowledge me in my misery.
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. The Duke and everyone who knows me in the city can witness with me that this isn't so. I've never seen Syracuse in my life.
DUKE. I tell you, Syracusan, for twenty years I've been patron to Antipholus, and during that time he never saw Syracuse. I see your age and dangers are making you delirious.
[Enter the Abbess with Antipholus of Syracuse and Dromio of Syracuse.]
ABBESS. Most mighty Duke, behold a man much wronged.
[All gather to see them.]
ADRIANA. I see two husbands — or my eyes deceive me.
DUKE. One of these men is the guardian-spirit of the other; and so of these — which is the natural man, and which the spirit? Who can tell them apart?
DROMIO OF SYRACUSE. I, sir, am Dromio — order him away.
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. I, sir, am Dromio — please let me stay.
ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE. Egeon — are you not? Or else his ghost?
DROMIO OF SYRACUSE. Oh, my old master — who has bound him here?

ABBESS. Whoever bound him, I'll loose his bonds, and gain a husband by his freedom. Speak, old Egeon, if you are the man who once had a wife called Emilia, who bore you in one delivery two fine sons. Oh, if you are the same Egeon, speak — and speak to the same Emilia!

DUKE. Why, here begins his morning story aright: these two Antipholuses, so alike, and these two Dromios, identical in appearance, besides her account of her shipwreck at sea. These are the parents of these children, who by accident are met together.
EGEON. If I'm not dreaming, you are Emilia. If you are she, tell me — where is the son that floated with you on the fatal raft?

ABBESS. By men of Epidamnum, he and I and the twin Dromio were all taken up. But soon after, rude fishermen of Corinth by force took Dromio and my son from them, and left me with those of Epidamnum. What became of them after that I cannot tell — only that I came to the fortune you see me in.
DUKE. Antipholus, you came from Corinth first?
ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE. No, sir, not I — I came from Syracuse.
DUKE. Wait, stand apart — I don't know which is which.
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. I came from Corinth, my most gracious lord.
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. And I with him.
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. Brought to this town by that most famous warrior, Duke Menaphon, your most renowned uncle.
ADRIANA. Which of you two dined with me today?
ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE. I did, gentle mistress.
ADRIANA. And aren't you my husband?
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. No, I say no to that.

ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE. And so do I — yet she did call me so; and this fair gentlewoman, her sister here, called me brother. What I told you then, I hope I'll have leisure to make good — if this isn't a dream I see and hear.
ANGELO. That is the chain, sir, that you had from me.
ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE. I think it is, sir. I don't deny it.
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. And you, sir, had me arrested for that chain.
ANGELO. I think I did, sir. I don't deny it.
ADRIANA. I sent you money, sir, for your bail, by Dromio — but I think he didn't bring it.
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. No, none by me.

ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE. This purse of ducats I received from you, and Dromio my man brought them to me. I see we kept meeting each other's servant, and I was taken for him, and he for me — and from that these mistakes arose.
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. These ducats I pledge for my father here.
DUKE. It won't be needed — your father has his life.
COURTESAN. Sir, I must have that diamond from you.
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. There, take it — and many thanks for my entertainment.

ABBESS. Renowned Duke, take the trouble to come with us into the abbey here, and hear at length all our fortunes recounted. And all who are gathered in this place, who through this sympathetic single day's confusion have suffered wrong, come, keep us company, and we'll make full restitution. Thirty-three years have I been in labour with you, my sons — and till this hour my heavy burden never delivered. The Duke, my husband, and both my children, and you, the calendars of their birth, come to a christening feast, and come with me. After such long grief, such a nativity.
DUKE. With all my heart, I'll be godfather at this feast.
[Exeunt except the two Dromios and two Brothers.]
DROMIO OF SYRACUSE. Master, shall I fetch your things from the ship?
ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS. Dromio, what things of mine have you put aboard?
DROMIO OF SYRACUSE. Your goods that lay at the inn, sir, at the Centaur.
ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE. He's speaking to me — I am your master, Dromio. Come, go with us. We'll see to that later. Embrace your brother there, rejoice with him.
[Exeunt Antipholus of Syracuse and Antipholus of Ephesus.]
DROMIO OF SYRACUSE. There's a fat friend at your master's house who kitchen-claimed me for you today at dinner. From now on she'll be my sister-in-law, not my wife.
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. I think you're my mirror, not my brother. I see by you that I'm a sweet-faced youth. Will you come in to watch their christening?
DROMIO OF SYRACUSE. Not I, sir — you're the elder.
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. That's the question — how shall we decide it?
DROMIO OF SYRACUSE. We'll draw lots for the senior. Till then, you lead.
DROMIO OF EPHESUS. No, then, like this: we came into the world like brother and brother, and now let's go hand in hand, neither before the other.
[Exeunt.]
